events.excerpt: GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That's around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. Users skipped doses, delayed getting refills, and used smaller doses than prescribed, among other changes. More than half of the people modifying how they used the drug said the changes w
events.headline: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed

events.excerpt: Prepared by: @Zecoshi Date: 13 November 2026 Status: Proposal for discussion Abstract Zcash is known as a private way to pay. This proposal argues that it can be something larger: the first public network able to protect records themselves, not only payments. Zcash Shielded Assets would let anyone issue an asset whose holdings and transfers are private while its total supply stays publicly provable. The specifications exist as drafts, but they are written for the Orchard pool, which no longer accepts new value, and they are not scheduled for any network upgrade. This proposal argues that shielded assets should be scheduled for a named upgrade, retargeted to the Ironwood pool, and covered by the same formal verification as Ironwood itself. events.excerpt: v2.11.1 is a security and stability release on top of v2.11.0 . It's the public release of v2.11.1-priv , which most validators already run. No hardfork, no config change, no database schema change, no resync required. Nodes can be upgraded one at a time, in any order. Highlights Stateless import : each block's header, and its body against the header, are checked before the block is executed. This applies to both the sequential and the parallel import path. Parallel import waits for a batch's header checks before it executes the batch. Execution and RPC : on a chain with no blob schedule, transaction pre-checks return ErrNoBlobBaseFee ( blob base fee unavailable ) for blob transactions. Operator notes Operators on v2.11.1-priv : same code, switch to v2.11.1 at your next maintenance window. Operators on v2.11.0 : upgrade. All operators should run this release. eth_simulateV1 calls that carry blob hashes return blob base fee unavailable unless the call overrides the blob base fee ( blockOverrides.blobBaseFee ). eth_call , eth_estimateGas and the tracers are unchanged. Unsurprisingly it’s easy enough to read and write this same NFC chip with a PN532 NFC reader and ESP32-S3 MCU. This reveals data fields for everything from brush type, to total runtime and expected lifetime, inviting a bit of experimentation on how certain usage patterns affects these data fields. This much is perhaps not too shocking, but the fun part is what you can do with the chip after you have figured out how to write to its memory. How to unlock these units and their NXP NTAG213 IC has been figured out a few years ago already, so the hardest part was to figure out what to do with this information. The demonstrated use case in the video is to unlock an Apple Macbook, which is maybe a bit too niche. Also demonstrated is taking the chip and its antenna out of the brush, which turns out to be quite easy. Microsoft alone added 1,094 security flaws to the total count on Tuesday, following 1,474 vulnerabilities the month before. “There's no denying the fact that vulnerability hunting with AI is driving a majority of what we're seeing.” All the major CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) - these are the organizations authorized by the CVE program to assign unique identifiers to security vulnerabilities - like VulnCheck, Microsoft, Oracle, GitHub, and other large enterprise IT vendors “are just screaming into the atmosphere right now,” Bressers said. “It’s AI.” Meanwhile, the percentage of these bugs that are exploited in the wild remains relatively consistent. LogicLens and Receipts claim to identify logical fallacies , flag reports that misrepresent information, detect content that attempts to polarize an issue, and the like. It also cites sources, so if, for example, you need to call someone out on their BS, you’ll have ammunition. Using the Chrome extension is as simple as clicking on its icon in the list of extensions in the browser. On iOS, the Receipts app is found as a share option. Once it starts, LogicLens scans an article, post, video, etc. to find potential issues of factual or logical inconsistency and flags them for review. events.excerpt: We introduced Kitesurf , our stateless browser for AI agents that runs entirely on top of Workers, in August and followed up in September with WebMCP support, new APIs, and improved compatibility. On every occasion, we mentioned our commitment to open sourcing it so that developers could run their own browser engine on their own Cloudflare accounts if they want to. That promise is now real. Kitesurf is open source on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license. You can read the code, run it locally, change it, and deploy your own instance to Cloudflare Workers. A browser built for agents Kitesurf runs entirely on Cloudflare Workers. It parses HTML, applies CSS, executes page JavaScript, and renders screenshots without a browser container. It supports the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), so you can connect clients such as Puppeteer. Our main goal is to give AI agents a lightweight, efficient browser — one that can load websites, execute JavaScript, and interact with pages while using less CPU and memory than a full browser like Chromium, and scaling on demand across Cloudflare’s global Workers network. events.excerpt: Elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time. Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured. Accidental savanna Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country's four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006). Read full article Comments
events.headline: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits

Bitcoin has fallen since the quarter closed on Sept. 30. The Texas firm’s coins are now worth about $700 million less than it paid. Where Did Twenty One Capital’s $1 Billion Profit Come From? US accounting rules require companies to book changes in the value of crypto they hold as profit or loss. No coins need to be sold. At the end of September, each Bitcoin was worth about $83,700, the company’s quarterly filing shows. That price lifted its 43,514 coins by $1.093 billion. Bitcoin Price Performance Since September 30. Source: TradingView Meanwhile, the business itself reported no revenue. It posted a $4.8 million operating loss for the quarter.
